intro: Everything you need to get from a fresh save to your first transcension in Clicker Heroes 1.0e12. It assumes an idle build, which is the easiest way to start: gold keeps accruing while the game is closed. Once you have transcended and picked up a few in-game auto-clickers, a hybrid or active build will take you further.

yourFirstRun.title: Your first run
yourFirstRun.summary: The first play-through is the slowest one you will ever do. Get to zone 130 and reset.

items.firstUpgrade: Level each hero to their first upgrade at level 10, then move on to the next hero.
items.laterUpgrades: Further down the roster, push to the level 25 upgrade before switching — and later, level 50.
items.allHeroUpgrades: Go back and buy the <link>all-hero DPS upgrades</link> whenever you can afford them.
items.lastUpgrade: Do not level heroes past their last upgrade yet.
items.failedBoss: Failed a boss? Farm gold on the previous zone until you can kill it.
items.longWaits: Expect long waits early on. Gold accumulates offline, so walking away for a while is a valid strategy.
items.skills: Fire every skill to punch through a boss wall, roughly every half hour.
items.primalBosses: Zones 110, 120 and 130 are all primal bosses, so each one is guaranteed Hero Souls.

whenToAscend.title: When to ascend
whenToAscend.summary: Ascension is the main progression loop. Each reset should be faster than the last.

items.moreSouls: The more Hero Souls you bank before ascending, the quicker the next run goes.
items.zone130: Get at least to zone 130 before your first ascension — it is a guaranteed primal boss.
items.every100th: Every 100th zone after that is also a guaranteed primal boss.
items.keepPushing: Keep pushing until you hit a boss you cannot kill. If it is primal, farm gold and try again before giving up on it.
items.spendGold: Spend leftover gold on hero levels right before you reset: every 2,000 combined hero levels is one extra Hero Soul. This stops mattering later, but the souls are worth having now.

beyondZone130.title: Beyond zone 130
beyondZone130.summary: From your second run onward, the Power 5 carry you.

items.backUp: Back up your save regularly to cloud storage, or just email the text file to yourself. You can pull a copy out at any time with the <link>save editor</link>.
items.power5: Level Frostleaf to 150, then go back to the top and level Treebeast, Ivan, Brittany, the Seer and the Masked Samurai — the “Power 5” — in multiples of 25.
items.remainingUpgrades: You can buy all remaining hero upgrades at this point too.
items.dreadKnight: Ignore Dread Knight. His cost-to-DPS ratio is terrible; what you actually want is the ×10 bonus for taking a hero to level 1000, and the Power 5 will serve for a long while.
items.buy25: After a few ascensions you will clear the early zones just by buying 25 hero levels at a time.
items.deGilding: Random de-gilding into the Power 5 is optional. If you do it, spend no more than 10% of your Hero Souls on it — and before your first transcension, do not bother moving gilds at all.

ancientsBeforeTranscending.title: Before transcending
ancientsBeforeTranscending.summary: Four ancients, kept level. Nothing else until you transcend.

items.idleFirst: Idle is the build to start with, because gold accrues while the game is closed.
items.buyFour: Buy Siyalatas, Libertas, Mammon and Mimzee, and no others, until your first transcension.
items.keepLevel: Keep all four at the same level, or as close to it as you can manage.
items.spareSouls: Hold unspent Hero Souls equal to the square of their level — level 5 ancients means keeping 25 Hero Souls spare.

ancientsAfterTranscending.title: After transcending
ancientsAfterTranscending.summary: Buy order is a rough ranking by usefulness, not a rule.

items.earlyPick: Get an idle ancient or Juggernaut as early as you can in a new transcension, depending on whether you are running idle or active/hybrid.
items.idleOrder: Buy first as idle: Libertas, Siyalatas, Nogardnit.
items.activeOrder: Buy first as active or hybrid: Juggernaut, Bhaal, Fragsworth.
items.next: Buy next: Atman, Kumawakamaru, then any gold ancients.
items.summonAll: Use “Summon All Ancients” once you can afford the remainder in one go.
items.nogardnit: Only level Nogardnit if you have in-game auto-clickers. Without them he does nothing.
items.calculator: Work out the actual levels with the <link>ancients calculator</link> — import your save and it returns optimal levels and costs for idle, hybrid or active.

yourFirstTranscension.title: Your first transcension
yourFirstTranscension.summary: Unlocks at zone 300. Do it immediately.

items.what: Transcendence is a second-tier reset that gets you moving again once ascensions stop producing meaningful gains.
items.lose: You give up ancients, relics, Hero Souls, zone gilds and zone progress.
items.keep: You keep Ancient Souls, rubies, outsiders, mercenaries, clan progress and any gilds bought with rubies.
items.outsiders: Ancient Souls are spent on the nine outsiders — meta-ancients, each with a different bonus, and respeccable for free every transcension.
items.transcendentPower: You also gain Transcendent Power, which exponentially increases the Hero Souls you get from primal bosses. That is why it is not worth grinding before your first transcension: take it at zone 300 and earn the souls back faster afterwards.
items.timing: To judge later transcensions, watch how fast your Hero Souls per ascension are growing. When the order of magnitude stops climbing, it is time to reset. The <link>transcension viewer</link> shows that history straight from your save.

spendingRubies.title: Spending rubies
spendingRubies.summary: Auto-clickers first, permanent damage second, everything else later.

items.autoClickers: Start with one or two auto-clickers, then the permanent double damage upgrade.
items.reserve: Keep a small reserve for reviving mercenaries while it is still cheap.
items.quickAscension: Quick Ascension is no longer needed at the start of a new transcension, thanks to the outsider Phandoryss.
items.moreAutoClickers: More auto-clickers come next; they scale exponentially once you have five.
items.timelapse: Timelapse becomes important tens of thousands of zones in. Use it at the start of a long ascension, with your gilds stacked and long ruby merc quests running.
items.avoid: Do not spend rubies on recruiting mercenaries, gilds, relics, or extra raid boss fights. None of them are worth it.

mercenaries.title: Mercenaries
mercenaries.summary: Free progress if you keep them questing. Ruby quests are the ones that matter.

items.lifespan: Every mercenary has a predetermined time until death, and only time spent on quests counts against it.
items.rewards: Quest rewards are multiplied by mercenary level, and 24 hours of quest time is one level.
items.revive: Revive them while it is cheap. Past level 11 or 12 the cost usually is not worth it.
items.questLength: Short quests pay better per minute; long quests need less babysitting but risk a high-level merc dying mid-quest.
items.rubyQuests: Ruby quests are the best. Hero Soul, gold, relic and skill quests are situational at best.
items.quality: Mercenary quality is pure RNG. Questing the ones you have beats cycling through hoping for better.

clans.title: Clans
clans.summary: A daily raid boss, and free Hero Souls for showing up.

items.raid: Fight a daily raid boss with up to nine other clan-mates.
items.reward: The minimum reward is 4 Hero Souls, and it scales up as you kill primal bosses.
items.join: Join a clan of players at a similar stage. The <link>r/ClickerHeroesRecruit subreddit</link> is the usual place to find one.

items.dwarfed: Every relic stat is eventually dwarfed by ancient levels, but they help in the early game.
items.bestStats: Kumawakamaru is the best stat overall. Atman and Revolc are fine too.
items.activeBuilds: On active or hybrid builds without infinite skill uptime, a good Sniperino or Klepto relic extends Lucky Strikes and Golden Clicks.

whereToGoNext.summary: Tools and references for once you are past your first transcension.
